name: comments
documentation: The Comments plugin — owns the comment.discussion domain: reader comments on a Plugins\Posts post. A comment may be submitted only when PostServiceContract::find($postId) returns a post whose status is 'published' AND commentsEnabled is true. Comments thread up to COMMENTS_MAX_DEPTH levels (default 3); a reply to an already-maximally-nested comment attaches to that comment's own parent instead of nesting further. Moderation status (pending | approved | spam | trash) is a STORED column — unlike Posts' computed status — decided by COMMENTS_MODERATION ('all' | 'first' | 'none') unless the submitter already holds the moderate permission, in which case the comment is auto-approved. A spam guard runs on every submission: a honeypot field and an excess of links in the body both silently resolve to the 'spam' status (never an error); a stale or too-fast signed form token, an unknown parent, and a repeated post+email+body within 10 minutes are all rejected with a 422; a per-IP-hash rate limit (CachePort, best-effort) is enforced both by the plugin's own comments.throttle route filter (HTTP 429, on the submit route) and inside the service itself (422), so a caller that invokes the published contract directly is still protected. The public read surface (thread/count/counts) returns ONLY approved comments and NEVER exposes an author's email, IP or user agent; the admin surface (list/find/moderate/update/delete/bulkModerate), gated by the plugin's own comments.moderate route filter (401 for a guest, 403 without COMMENTS_MODERATE_PERMISSION), may show the email. Rows live in the request's database — the migration ships in both database/migrations and database/tenant-template, so the plugin works with or without Tenancy. Routes: GET/POST /api/comments/posts/{postId}, GET /api/comments/form-token, and the admin CRUD under /api/admin/comments (deliberately NOT under /api/posts, to avoid colliding with Posts' own /api/posts/{kind}/{slug} route).
